subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Kilonovae: Cosmic Gold Factories
description: Learn Kilonovae: Cosmic Gold Factories in one minute.

hook.text: A kilonova is the explosive aftermath of two neutron stars merging—a brilliant flash that lasts just days.

buildup.text: The merger ejects neutron-rich debris at a fraction of light speed. Rapid neutron capture builds heavy elements almost instantly.

discovery.text: The 2017 kilonova from GW170817 was observed across the spectrum. It produced an estimated 10 Earth-masses of gold.

twist.text: Before this observation, nobody knew where most gold and platinum came from. Kilonovae answered a decades-old question.

climax.text: Each kilonova creates more precious metals than exist on Earth. They are the universe's ultimate alchemy events.

punchline.text: Ten Earth-masses of gold from one collision. Cosmic alchemy in a flash of light.

quiz.question: What major question did the 2017 kilonova observation answer?
options: Where most of the universe's gold and platinum come from—neutron star mergers
Whether gravitational waves travel at the speed of light
How black holes form from the merger of two neutron stars

details.summary: A kilonova is the optical and infrared glow produced when neutron star mergers eject material rich in newly forged heavy elements. The radioactive decay of these elements powers a days-to-weeks-long glow roughly 1,000 times brighter than ordinary novae — hence the name.
details.whyItMatters: Kilonovae revealed where the universe's heaviest elements come from. Observing them confirmed decades of theoretical predictions about r-process nucleosynthesis and connected gravitational wave signals to visible light.
takeaways: Optical glow from heavy elements forged in neutron star mergers
About 1,000 times brighter than a typical nova
They are the primary source of heavy elements like gold

faq.question: How were kilonovae first observed?
faq.answer: The first confirmed kilonova was associated with GW170817 in 2017. Within hours of the gravitational wave detection, telescopes found a new optical source in galaxy NGC 4993. It faded from blue to red over days as heavier elements cooled — matching kilonova predictions beautifully.

faq.question: What elements are produced in kilonovae?
faq.answer: Rapid neutron capture (r-process) elements: everything from strontium to uranium. The neutron-rich ejecta captures neutrons faster than radioactive decay can occur, building up the heaviest stable and radioactive elements. This includes gold, platinum, iodine, and thorium.
